clue.text: Wide, large prison for the strumpet's child

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for large
BIRD is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime = time

explanation.surface: A rough description of a big jail where a prostitute's child is held.
explanation.walkthrough: A wosbird is an old dialect word for an illegitimate child, which explains the 'strumpet's child'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic dialect insult for a bastard, which is literally the offspring of a loose woman.

clue.text: Bubbly dowager?

definitions.meaning: champagne, from the famous Veuve (French for this) Clicquot brand
a dowager is a titled woman whose husband has died

explanation.walkthrough: Veuve Clicquot champagne is nicknamed by its first word, French for a bereaved wife, so 'Bubbly' gives the same word as 'dowager'.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is nicknamed after Veuve Clicquot, and a dowager is a woman who has lost her husband.

clue.text: Note the song where would-be Brownies camp?

parts.note: SOL (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A singing session at a Girl Guides' junior camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies are junior Girl Guides, but here they are people wanting a suntan, who lie in sunrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunrooms or sun terraces are places where people sit to get brown, playfully called would-be Brownies.

clue.text: Expedition suggested in Macbeth soliloquy: "Interned wretch! Renowned idle wee twit! We knife thee painfully!"

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Interned wretch! Renowned idle wee twit! We knife thee painfully!' does not anagram to IF IT WERE DONE WHEN 'TIS DONE THEN 'TWERE WELL IT WERE DONE QUICKLY: with 'painfully' the fodder has N,F,P,A where the answer needs O,O,S,Q; without it, plus 'Expedition' as QUICKLY, it has C,K for O,O,S,L. No source found to correct it.

clue.text: See 3
Farceur fails to close a Scottish theatre

indicators.note: something that fails to close does not reach its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the Traverse is a theatre in Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A comic writer of farces cannot keep a Scottish playhouse open.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Travers wrote the Aldwych farces of the 1920s; the Traverse is Edinburgh's new-writing theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Travers was a celebrated English writer of stage farces, so he is a farceur by profession.

clue.text: See 3
He counselled David with a greeting, tho' help failed

parts.note: HI is an informal word of welcome
taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: failed means these words have broken down and come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An adviser to the king said hello, though his help came to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' rearranges HELP into PHEL. Ahithophel was David's counsellor who joined Absalom's revolt (2 Samuel).
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible this man was King David's counsellor who later sided with Absalom's revolt.

clue.text: Endless reliance could be redundant at Bletchley Park?

indicators.note: could be signals that the remaining letters can be rearranged into something else
endless means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Total dependence might prove unnecessary at the wartime codebreaking centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts RELIANCE to RELIANC, and 'could be' rearranges it. Bletchley Park was Britain's wartime codebreaking centre, where messages already in plain text needed no breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A message sent in plain language, not in code, would need no work from codebreakers.

clue.text: Spot moose mushrooms rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: the elk is the European name for the moose
ceps are edible boletus mushrooms

explanation.surface: Catching sight of a moose among mushrooms that are springing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the whole run ELKCEPS upwards, so it reads SPECKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A speckle is a small spot or mark, and as a noun the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Flirting with daughter before marriage

parts.note: an alliance is a union by marriage between families

explanation.surface: A young woman flirts with someone ahead of her wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance is casual romantic play, a noun close in sense to flirting used as a noun.

clue.text: Linen tape used in drain cleaning

indicators.note: used in says the answer sits inside the following words, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: Fabric tape is employed in clearing out a blocked drain.
explanation.definitionFit: Incle is a woven linen tape used for trimming and binding, an old haberdashery word.

clue.text: See 3
Horsewhip the defender with the up and over line

parts.note: to switch is to whip with a thin flexible cane
a back is a defensive player in football or hockey

explanation.surface: A jockey whips a defender at a racetrack line.
explanation.walkthrough: The switchback is a fairground ride or mountain railway whose track climbs and dips repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchback is a roller-coaster style railway whose track goes up and over repeated humps.

clue.text: Male office worker in match play

indicators.note: in places the male and the office worker inside the match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
HE is the male pronoun
a temp is a temporary office worker

explanation.surface: A man working in an office takes part in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late romance set on Prospero's island is one of his best-known plays.

clue.text: Pinhead? Not I! Might be her!

indicators.note: might be signals that the remaining letters could form another word
Not I tells the solver to remove the letter I from the word before

parts.note: I is the letter itself

explanation.surface: Someone denies being a fool and points at a woman instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes I from PINHEAD, leaving PNHEAD, which 'Might be' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, here standing for any female person named in the clue as 'her'.

clue.text: One-sided celebration, say, for divorcées

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: say tells the solver that a word spoken sounds like the letters entered

parts.note: a party is a celebration

explanation.surface: A celebration thrown for divorced women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks PARTY as spoken, giving PARTE. Ex parte is the legal Latin for a hearing at which only one side is present.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal Latin for proceedings brought on behalf of only one party, hence partial or one-sided.

clue.text: James's valet joining alien group

parts.note: Peter Quint is the dead valet in Henry James's The Turn of the Screw
ET is the extraterrestrial of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A novelist's manservant joins a band of extraterrestrials.
explanation.definitionFit: A quintet is a set of five performers or things, so it is a kind of group.

clue.text: See 3
African, Welshman and Scotsman

parts.note: Ivor is a typical Welsh first name
Ian is a typical Scottish first name

explanation.surface: Three nationalities line up, as in the opening of a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Côte d'Ivoire in West Africa is called by this demonym.

clue.text: Ecstasy absorbed by old soak returning from college

indicators.note: absorbed by means the drug's letter is taken inside the other pieces

parts.note: EX means former or old

indicators.note: returning means the word for soak is read backwards

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax to soften it
E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A former drunkard full of ecstasy comes back from university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' looks like a drunkard, but it is the flax-workers' verb, to soften flax by steeping; 'returning' and 'absorbed by' then finish the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter College is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: "My Way" sung on this journey?

parts.note: the Sinatra song about doing things one's own way suits a trip taken purely for self-gratification

explanation.walkthrough: My Way is Frank Sinatra's anthem of self-regard, which suits an indulgence undertaken to boost one's own vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: An activity pursued mainly to flatter oneself, an idiom built on the travel image.

clue.text: Abraham Darby's remains rot, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The body of a historic industrialist is decaying, regrettably.
explanation.walkthrough: Abraham Darby pioneered smelting iron with coke at Coalbrookdale; the definition reads 'Abraham Darby is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Darby owned and ran an iron foundry, so he was a manufacturer of iron.

clue.text: See 3
Good type resettled Israelites here

indicators.note: resettled means the letters are moved into new places

explanation.surface: A decent sort relocated the Hebrews to this place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israelites lived in this land in bondage before the Exodus, so this is where they were.

clue.text: Tell them to go for cabbage!

indicators.note: Tell means say aloud, so the word spoken is entered by its sound

parts.note: shoo is what you say to send animals or people away

explanation.surface: An order to drive someone off for the sake of a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: CHOU, French for cabbage, is said like SHOO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the French word for cabbage, also seen in chou pastry.

clue.text: Weapon thrown back by oriental informer

indicators.note: thrown back means the letters run in reverse order

parts.note: E for east, the oriental direction
a fink is an American slang word for a police informer

explanation.surface: An eastern spy hurls a blade backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade carried for fighting or stabbing is a classic weapon.

clue.text: Wilde, aka "frothy ale brewer"

indicators.note: a brewer stirs and mixes ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde was also known as a maker of foamy beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde's full name was Oscar Fingal O'Flahertie Wills Wilde.
explanation.definitionFit: Part of the writer's full baptismal name, so it is another name he had.

clue.text: Stan Getz failing? No way! First, there's a yen to see him in flower!

indicators.note: first places the yen's letter at the front

parts.note: Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

indicators.note: failing means the letters fall apart and are rearranged
no way means take away the letters for a road

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A jazz saxophonist falls short, and someone longs to see him in bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes ST from STANGETZ, and 'failing' rearranges ANGETZ. A 'flower' is a river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword sense of a river as a thing that flows, and this is China's longest river.

clue.text: Offensive about bum notes from this

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was a 1968 Vietnam War campaign
rump is a word for the backside, as is bum

explanation.surface: An attack on wrong notes played by a brass instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum notes' looks like one phrase, but 'bum' is wordplay and 'notes from this' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass instrument is the source of notes, so the answer is what the notes come from.
